name: Petra Croton
description: Codiaeum variegatum 'Petra' is a popular croton cultivar prized for its bold, glossy foliage. Broad pointed-oval leaves are dark green with bright yellow, orange, pink, and red veins, creating a colorful, almost lacy look from a distance. Native to southern Asia, Indonesia, and the eastern Pacific as a species, crotons thrive in bright light, warm temperatures, and moderate to high humidity. Indoors, Petra typically reaches about 0.9–1.8 m tall with an upright shrub habit. Color intensity depends on light—too little green fades the variegation; harsh midday sun can scorch leaves. Like other Euphorbiaceae, the milky sap is irritating and the plant is toxic if ingested, so handle with care and keep away from pets and children.
careTips: Give bright, indirect light (at least 4 hours daily); some gentle morning sun helps keep leaf colors vivid
Water when the top 2–3 cm of soil feels dry; keep evenly moist in the growing season and reduce watering in winter
Use a rich, well-draining mix; avoid soggy soil to prevent root rot
Maintain 50–70% humidity; mist, use a pebble tray, or place near a humidifier in dry rooms
Keep temperatures warm and stable (about 18–28 °C); protect from cold drafts below 15 °C
Wipe leaves occasionally to remove dust and check for spider mites, scale, and mealybugs
Propagate from stem cuttings in warm, humid conditions
Toxic if ingested and sap can irritate skin—wear gloves and keep away from pets and children

parentSpecies.name: Garden Croton
parentSpecies.description: Codiaeum variegatum is a tropical evergreen shrub in the Euphorbiaceae family, native to southern Asia, Indonesia, and the eastern Pacific islands. It is grown for its highly variable, colorful foliage and is the parent species of many popular houseplant cultivars, including 'Petra'. Plants prefer bright light, warm temperatures, and consistently moist but well-drained soil. All parts contain irritating milky sap and are toxic if ingested.
careTips: Bright light for best leaf color; avoid prolonged deep shade
Keep soil moist but not waterlogged; reduce watering in cooler months
Provide warm conditions and moderate to high humidity
Toxic if ingested; sap can irritate skin
